slides.title: When to change from IV to oral therapy
slides.section: When to change from IV to oral therapy
paragraphs: Oral therapy is reasonable when the patient is improving, source control is adequate, the organism is susceptible, the chosen drug reaches the relevant site and systemic exposure, the gastrointestinal tract works, and the patient can take the regimen reliably. “Bacteremia” by itself is not an indication for prolonged IV therapy.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
When to change from IV to oral therapy Oral therapy is reasonable when the patient is improving, source control is adequate, the organism is susceptible, the chosen drug reaches the relevant site and systemic exposure, the gastrointestinal tract works, and the patient can take the regimen reliably. “Bacteremia” by itself is not an indication for prolonged IV therapy. Agents with high oral exposure Fluoroquinolones, linezolid, metronidazole, TMP-SMX, doxycycline, and fluconazole have high oral bioavailability. Oral beta-lactams can also work for selected infections. Check the dose, organism MIC, infection site, and supporting clinical evidence. When IV therapy should continue Hemodynamic instability, uncontrolled source, unreliable absorption, no active oral option, endovascular or CNS infection without a validated oral strategy, adherence barriers that cannot be addressed, or a clinical course that does not fit the presumed diagnosis. Approximate oral absorption and urinary excretion for common cUTI options Agent Oral absorption Urinary excretion Amoxicillin-clavulanate Amoxicillin about 80%; clavulanate variable Amoxicillin 50–70%; clavulanate 25–40% Cefixime About 50% About 50% Cefpodoxime About 50% About 30% Ceftibuten 75–90% About 56% Cefuroxime About 52% About 50% Cephalexin About 90% About 90% Ciprofloxacin About 70% 40–50% Levofloxacin About 99% 64–100% TMP-SMX 70–90% Sulfamethoxazole 84%; trimethoprim 66% Values are approximate and come from the dosing supplement to the 2025 IDSA cUTI guideline. 2 Absorption is not the same as adequate exposure. Dose, organism MIC, infection site, renal function, and clinical evidence still determine whether an oral drug is a reasonable choice. Oral therapy for uncomplicated gram-negative bacteremia. The 2021 Delphi guidance favored fluoroquinolones or TMP-SMX when active and allowed selected oral beta-lactams only when pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic target attainment was likely with optimized dosing. It raised specific concerns about routinely using cefadroxil, cefpodoxime, or cefdinir for this purpose. It is not a local dosing table. Use the current institutional pathway, susceptibility report, syndrome, and pharmacy input for patient-specific decisions. 38 Source control. Changing to oral therapy does not compensate for inadequate drainage, debridement, device management, or relief of obstruction. These are often the conditions that allow either oral or IV therapy to succeed.

paragraphs: Each trial evaluated a specific population and treatment strategy. Apply the inclusion criteria and exclusions before using the result at the bedside.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Selected trials Each trial evaluated a specific population and treatment strategy. Apply the inclusion criteria and exclusions before using the result at the bedside. MERINO Harris et al., 2018. In 378 patients with ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli or K. pneumoniae bloodstream infection, 30-day mortality was 12.3% with piperacillin-tazobactam and 3.7% with meropenem. Piperacillin-tazobactam did not meet noninferiority. Prefer a carbapenem for invasive ESBL infection even when piperacillin-tazobactam is reported susceptible. 7 CAMERA2 Tong et al., 2020. slides.title: POET
paragraphs: Iversen et al., 2019. Four hundred stable adults with selected left-sided endocarditis due to streptococci, E. faecalis , S. aureus , or coagulase-negative staphylococci were randomized after at least 10 days of IV therapy. The composite outcome occurred in 9.0% with partial oral therapy and 12.1% with continued IV therapy. The conclusion applies to carefully selected, stable patients using protocolized combination regimens and close follow-up, not to routine early oral treatment of endocarditis. 10
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Selected trials Each trial evaluated a specific population and treatment strategy. Apply the inclusion criteria and exclusions before using the result at the bedside. MERINO Harris et al., 2018. In 378 patients with ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli or K. pneumoniae bloodstream infection, 30-day mortality was 12.3% with piperacillin-tazobactam and 3.7% with meropenem. Piperacillin-tazobactam did not meet noninferiority. Prefer a carbapenem for invasive ESBL infection even when piperacillin-tazobactam is reported susceptible. 7 CAMERA2 Tong et al., 2020. Adding 7 days of an antistaphylococcal beta-lactam to vancomycin or daptomycin for MRSA bacteremia did not improve the primary composite outcome. It reduced persistent bacteremia at day 5 but increased acute kidney injury from 6% to 23%, and the trial stopped early. This does not support routine combination therapy. 8 OVIVA Li et al., 2019. Among 1,054 adults with bone, joint, or orthopedic hardware infection, an oral strategy used during the first 6 weeks was noninferior to continued IV therapy. Definite treatment failure occurred in 13.2% of the oral group and 14.6% of the IV group among patients with endpoint data. IV catheter complications were much more frequent with IV therapy. Oral drugs were selected by infection specialists; this was not evidence that any oral agent is adequate for any bone infection. 9 POET Iversen et al., 2019. slides.title: Presenting the antibiotic plan on rounds
slides.section: Presenting the antibiotic plan on rounds
paragraphs: The primary team should be able to tell what you think is being treated, why this drug was chosen, what still needs to happen, and when the plan will change.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Presenting the antibiotic plan on rounds The primary team should be able to tell what you think is being treated, why this drug was chosen, what still needs to happen, and when the plan will change. Syndrome and source [What infection are we treating? Is the source controlled?] Microbiology [Relevant cultures, susceptibilities, and prior organisms] Antibiotic decision today [Drug and route] because [coverage, site, host, and resistance considerations] Safety and dosing [Renal/hepatic adjustment, allergy, interaction, and monitoring plan] Reassessment [What pending result or clinical change permits narrowing, oral transition, stopping, or additional source evaluation?] Duration [First day of effective therapy or other duration anchor, anticipated stop date, and reason] Common errors Fever is treated as a diagnosis without establishing an infectious syndrome. Vancomycin and an antipseudomonal beta-lactam are continued after cultures and the clinical course allow narrowing. MSSA remains on vancomycin instead of an active antistaphylococcal beta-lactam. Susceptible Klebsiella is treated broadly because its narrower beta-lactam options were never reviewed. Fluoroquinolones are rejected categorically even when they provide the best susceptible oral option for cUTI or Pseudomonas . Renal function changes without a dosing reassessment, particularly with cefepime, vancomycin, aminoglycosides, TMP-SMX, or fluoroquinolones. A PICC is ordered before anyone asks whether a validated oral regimen is available. The drug is changed repeatedly while an abscess, obstruction, infected catheter, or hardware remains untreated.

slides.title: Questions for the end of the session
slides.section: Questions for the end of the session
paragraphs: 1. A ceftriaxone-susceptible K. pneumoniae urine and blood isolate is improving after urinary decompression. Must cefepime be continued?
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Questions for the end of the session 1. A ceftriaxone-susceptible K. pneumoniae urine and blood isolate is improving after urinary decompression. Must cefepime be continued? Answer No. If there is no ESBL or other resistance concern and the patient is improving, ceftriaxone is a reasonable narrower IV option. Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin may be reasonable orally when susceptible and otherwise appropriate. 2. Which oral antibiotics can be relied on for susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa ? Answer Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin. Fluoroquinolones are the only established oral class with reliable antipseudomonal activity. Confirm susceptibility. Moxifloxacin is not an appropriate substitute. 3. What should be checked when a service uses trough monitoring for vancomycin? Answer If the service uses trough monitoring, confirm the correct draw time, follow serum creatinine, and use the indication-specific target in the local pharmacy workflow. The national 2020 consensus recommends AUC-guided monitoring for serious MRSA infection, and local monitoring practices may differ. 4. Does OVIVA show that every osteomyelitis patient can receive any active oral antibiotic from day 1? Answer No. Patients entered a specialist-directed oral strategy within 7 days of definitive surgery or planned curative treatment. Drug selection, source control, diagnosis, absorption, adherence, and follow-up still matter. 5. What should happen when cultures narrow the likely pathogen? Answer Reassess whether infection is present, narrow to the least broad effective drug, confirm the dose and route, address source control, and establish the duration anchor and stop date. Sometimes the correct decision is to stop antibiotics. 6. Fellow extension: An Enterobacterales isolate produces NDM. Is ceftazidime-avibactam alone a reliable choice? Answer No. Avibactam does not inhibit NDM, and NDM hydrolyzes ceftazidime. Current IDSA guidance lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is unavailable. Final selection still depends on susceptibility testing, infection site, clinical stability, source control, and local ID pharmacy input.

slides.title: Answer
slides.section: Questions for the end of the session
paragraphs: If the service uses trough monitoring, confirm the correct draw time, follow serum creatinine, and use the indication-specific target in the local pharmacy workflow. The national 2020 consensus recommends AUC-guided monitoring for serious MRSA infection, and local monitoring practices may differ.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Questions for the end of the session 1. A ceftriaxone-susceptible K. pneumoniae urine and blood isolate is improving after urinary decompression. Must cefepime be continued? Answer No. If there is no ESBL or other resistance concern and the patient is improving, ceftriaxone is a reasonable narrower IV option. Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin may be reasonable orally when susceptible and otherwise appropriate. 2. Which oral antibiotics can be relied on for susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa ? Answer Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin. Fluoroquinolones are the only established oral class with reliable antipseudomonal activity. Confirm susceptibility. Moxifloxacin is not an appropriate substitute. 3. What should be checked when a service uses trough monitoring for vancomycin? Answer If the service uses trough monitoring, confirm the correct draw time, follow serum creatinine, and use the indication-specific target in the local pharmacy workflow. The national 2020 consensus recommends AUC-guided monitoring for serious MRSA infection, and local monitoring practices may differ. 4. Does OVIVA show that every osteomyelitis patient can receive any active oral antibiotic from day 1? Answer No. Patients entered a specialist-directed oral strategy within 7 days of definitive surgery or planned curative treatment. Drug selection, source control, diagnosis, absorption, adherence, and follow-up still matter. 5. What should happen when cultures narrow the likely pathogen? Answer Reassess whether infection is present, narrow to the least broad effective drug, confirm the dose and route, address source control, and establish the duration anchor and stop date. Sometimes the correct decision is to stop antibiotics. 6. Fellow extension: An Enterobacterales isolate produces NDM. Is ceftazidime-avibactam alone a reliable choice? Answer No. Avibactam does not inhibit NDM, and NDM hydrolyzes ceftazidime. Current IDSA guidance lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is unavailable. Final selection still depends on susceptibility testing, infection site, clinical stability, source control, and local ID pharmacy input.

slides.section: Questions for the end of the session
paragraphs: 5. What should happen when cultures narrow the likely pathogen?
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Questions for the end of the session 1. A ceftriaxone-susceptible K. pneumoniae urine and blood isolate is improving after urinary decompression. Must cefepime be continued? Answer No. If there is no ESBL or other resistance concern and the patient is improving, ceftriaxone is a reasonable narrower IV option. Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin may be reasonable orally when susceptible and otherwise appropriate. 2. Which oral antibiotics can be relied on for susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa ? Answer Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin. Fluoroquinolones are the only established oral class with reliable antipseudomonal activity. Confirm susceptibility. Moxifloxacin is not an appropriate substitute. 3. What should be checked when a service uses trough monitoring for vancomycin? Answer If the service uses trough monitoring, confirm the correct draw time, follow serum creatinine, and use the indication-specific target in the local pharmacy workflow. The national 2020 consensus recommends AUC-guided monitoring for serious MRSA infection, and local monitoring practices may differ. 4. Does OVIVA show that every osteomyelitis patient can receive any active oral antibiotic from day 1? Answer No. Patients entered a specialist-directed oral strategy within 7 days of definitive surgery or planned curative treatment. Drug selection, source control, diagnosis, absorption, adherence, and follow-up still matter. 5. What should happen when cultures narrow the likely pathogen? Answer Reassess whether infection is present, narrow to the least broad effective drug, confirm the dose and route, address source control, and establish the duration anchor and stop date. Sometimes the correct decision is to stop antibiotics. 6. Fellow extension: An Enterobacterales isolate produces NDM. Is ceftazidime-avibactam alone a reliable choice? Answer No. Avibactam does not inhibit NDM, and NDM hydrolyzes ceftazidime. Current IDSA guidance lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is unavailable. Final selection still depends on susceptibility testing, infection site, clinical stability, source control, and local ID pharmacy input.

slides.title: For fellows
paragraphs: Separate guideline recommendations from trial evidence and local practice. When several drugs are active, weigh resistance mechanism, inoculum, exposure, toxicity, source control, and the consequences of failure.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Before choosing the drug When someone asks, “What antibiotic should we use?” I usually need several other answers first. Sometimes the correct response is immediate broad therapy. Sometimes it is a better culture, drainage, or no antibiotic at all. Is there an infection? What findings support infection rather than colonization, inflammation, aspiration pneumonitis, or a contaminated specimen? How sick is the patient? Instability lowers the tolerance for missing a pathogen. A stable patient allows more diagnostic precision. Where is it? The syndrome determines likely organisms, penetration, source control, and duration. What has grown before? Review prior cultures, recent antibiotics, healthcare exposure, devices, and the local antibiogram. What will fix the source? Drainage, debridement, device removal, or relief of obstruction may matter more than adding another drug. When will we reassess? Write what you expect to know in 24–72 hours and what would allow narrowing or stopping. For students and residents Be able to state the syndrome, likely organisms, why the chosen drug covers them, what it misses, and what information will change the plan. For fellows Separate guideline recommendations from trial evidence and local practice. When several drugs are active, weigh resistance mechanism, inoculum, exposure, toxicity, source control, and the consequences of failure. A practical word about dosing Do not memorize one dose for each drug. The same antibiotic may have different doses for cystitis, bacteremia, meningitis, obesity, augmented renal clearance, intermittent hemodialysis, or continuous renal replacement therapy. Loading doses are often based on volume of distribution and may still be needed in acute kidney injury; maintenance dosing is where renal clearance usually matters. For severe infection, verify the dose before the first administration rather than waiting for the next day’s rounds. Local practice: Beta-lactam infusion practices differ across sites and may change. Do not assume standard or extended infusion from this module. Use the current site-specific order set and pharmacy guidance.

slides.title: Newer and restricted gram-negative agents
paragraphs: Optional fellow detail
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Newer and restricted gram-negative agents These drugs are restricted and are usually selected with ID and pharmacy input. Residents do not need to memorize which beta-lactamase each inhibitor blocks. Know the names, the broad clinical role, the major coverage gaps, and what information the consultant needs: organism, infection site, complete susceptibility results, prior antibiotics, and source-control status. 1 What residents should recognize on the medication list Agent Why it may be used What to remember Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Selected carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and some resistant Pseudomonas . It does not cover every resistance mechanism and is not reliable alone for NDM. It also lacks dependable anaerobic, MRSA, and enterococcal coverage. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Primarily susceptible, highly resistant Pseudomonas . It is not the default drug for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and is not a complete regimen for a polymicrobial infection. Meropenem-vaborbactam Vabomere Imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam Recarbrio Selected carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales. Imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam may also be used for susceptible DTR Pseudomonas . Do not treat these agents as interchangeable. Vaborbactam adds little activity against the usual resistance mechanisms in DTR Pseudomonas ; relebactam can restore imipenem activity in some isolates. Check susceptibility and involve ID pharmacy. Cefiderocol Fetroja Selected infections caused by highly resistant aerobic gram-negative organisms. It has no useful gram-positive or anaerobic activity, and susceptibility is not universal. Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo or ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam Selected Enterobacterales with NDM or another metallo-beta-lactamase. These are specialist regimens. They do not provide dependable gram-positive or anaerobic coverage. Aztreonam alone is not an adequate substitute. Sulbactam-durlobactam Xacduro Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii , usually with imipenem-cilastatin or meropenem. 1 34 Its role is specific to resistant Acinetobacter . It is not a CRE or resistant Pseudomonas drug. Why not meropenem-vaborbactam for DTR Pseudomonas ? Vaborbactam primarily inhibits class A enzymes, especially KPC, but does not correct OprD porin loss, increased efflux, or metallo-beta-lactamase production, important causes of carbapenem resistance in P. aeruginosa . It generally provides little additional activity over meropenem against this organism. For susceptible DTR Pseudomonas , consider ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, or imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam according to infection site and susceptibility; cefiderocol has an important role for metallo-beta-lactamase producers. Do not infer activity from the drug class alone. 1 Resident expectation: explain the organism, infection site, susceptibility results, source-control status, and why a restricted drug is being considered. Selection, dosing, and enzyme-level matching should be reviewed with ID pharmacy or an experienced ID consultant. Residents may continue to other commonly used inpatient agents ; the next section is optional fellow detail. Optional fellow detail

slides.title: Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents
paragraphs: This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

rows: Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents
rows: Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents
rows: Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents
rows: The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.
