slides.title: Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents
rows: A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance
Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Newer oral options and pipeline evidence
paragraphs: For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract.
Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Approved oral agents: labeling details
paragraphs: Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Choosing among restricted gram-negative agents This section is intended for fellows and residents seeking additional detail. Fellows should be able to compare agents by resistance mechanism, infection site, susceptibility result, prior exposure, and evidence. Confirm formulary restrictions and current susceptibility data before use. Drug-specific selection and limitations Agent Where it may fit Main limitation Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz A preferred option for KPC-producing Enterobacterales and the preferred option for OXA-48-like Enterobacterales. It is also one option for susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas . 1 14 Avibactam does not inhibit metallo-beta-lactamases such as NDM, VIM, or IMP. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone should not be assumed active against an NDM-producing isolate. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Its main niche is susceptible difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa . The 2026 IDSA guidance gives it preference for DTR Pseudomonas pneumonia. It also has ESBL activity, but broader reserve agents are generally preserved when a carbapenem or an active oral drug is adequate. 1 15 It is not a dependable solution for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, and susceptibility should not be inferred from the organism name. Cefiderocol Fetroja A siderophore cephalosporin with activity against some highly resistant Enterobacterales and nonfermenters. Current guidance includes it among preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales and metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas , and in selected roles for CRAB and invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia . 1 16 Activity is not universal, and clinical evidence remains limited for several of these organisms. The label retains a warning about an observed mortality imbalance in a trial involving carbapenem-resistant gram-negative infections. Confirm susceptibility before use. Aztreonam A traditional monobactam active only against susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms, including some Pseudomonas . It is stable to hydrolysis by metallo-beta-lactamases, which becomes useful when paired with an inhibitor that blocks commonly co-produced serine beta-lactamases. Aztreonam alone is often hydrolyzed by ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes that travel with NDM and other MBLs. It is not a reliable MBL regimen by itself and is usually a poor empiric agent because it has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity and gram-negative susceptibility cannot be assumed. Avoid routine empiric use. Penicillin allergy alone generally does not preclude aztreonam. Ceftazidime shares an identical R1 side chain, and clinical cross-reactivity has been reported. With a convincing immediate or severe ceftazidime reaction, clarify the phenotype and follow the local allergy pathway before using aztreonam. 4 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo The fixed combination protects aztreonam from many co-produced serine beta-lactamases. IDSA lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales, with a slight preference for aztreonam-avibactam. FDA labeling is narrower: adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection, given with metronidazole, who have limited or no alternatives. 1 17 It has limited activity against MBL-producing Pseudomonas , and there are no FDA or CLSI breakpoints for that organism. Several mechanism-based uses in IDSA guidance extend beyond the FDA indication. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam An alternative for NDM-producing Enterobacterales when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is not available. Avibactam protects aztreonam from the accompanying serine beta-lactamases while aztreonam avoids hydrolysis by NDM. 1 The combination requires coordinated dosing, renal adjustment, microbiology support, and ID pharmacy review. Current guidance slightly favors the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product when available. Coverage gaps with newer gram-negative agents A beta-lactamase inhibitor usually protects or extends the gram-negative activity of its partner beta-lactam. It does not add anaerobic, MRSA, enterococcal, or atypical coverage unless the partner drug already provides it. Sulbactam has intrinsic activity against Acinetobacter . What may still need to be added when the syndrome is polymicrobial Agent Anaerobes Gram-positive organisms Clinical implication Ceftazidime-avibactam Avycaz Do not rely on it for clinically adequate anaerobic coverage. The FDA-labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes concurrent metronidazole. 14 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy when required by the syndrome. Ceftolozane-tazobactam Zerbaxa Do not use it as stand-alone anaerobic therapy. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen includes metronidazole. 15 Do not count on it for MRSA or enterococci. Its primary role is treatment of susceptible resistant Pseudomonas . Cefiderocol Fetroja It is an aerobic gram-negative agent; add anaerobic therapy when the syndrome requires it. 16 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. A susceptible result does not make it a complete regimen for aspiration, bowel perforation, diabetic foot infection, or another mixed infection. Aztreonam No clinically useful anaerobic activity. No clinically useful gram-positive activity. Use only for susceptible aerobic gram-negative organisms. Alone, it may fail against an NDM isolate when ESBL, AmpC, KPC, or OXA enzymes are also present. Aztreonam and ceftazidime share an identical R1 side chain, so a ceftazidime allergy requires review. 21 Aztreonam-avibactam Emblaveo Do not rely on it for anaerobes. Its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen requires concurrent metronidazole. 17 Do not count on it for gram-positive coverage. Add metronidazole for its labeled complicated intra-abdominal infection regimen. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam The combination does not supply dependable anaerobic coverage. The combination does not supply dependable MRSA or enterococcal coverage. Add coverage for the remaining pathogens when the syndrome requires it. Add anaerobic or gram-positive therapy only when the syndrome, likely pathogens, and infection site require it. Obtain source control and narrow once cultures and the clinical course permit. Using the resistance mechanism to choose among active agents Fellows should connect the resistance phenotype to the likely enzyme, recognize when expected spectrum and measured susceptibility diverge, and explain why one active drug may be preferred over another. Review difficult isolates with microbiology and stewardship. Use the mechanism to narrow the list, then use the site and susceptibility result to choose Resistance problem Agents to discuss Main caution KPC-producing Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam, meropenem-vaborbactam, or imipenem-relebactam Choose by infection site, susceptibility, prior exposure, and local availability. OXA-48-like Enterobacterales Ceftazidime-avibactam Meropenem-vaborbactam and imipenem-relebactam are not reliable OXA-48 solutions. NDM or another MBL in Enterobacterales Aztreonam-avibactam or cefiderocol. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed product is unavailable. Ceftazidime-avibactam alone does not inhibit the MBL. DTR Pseudomonas aeruginosa Ceftolozane-tazobactam, ceftazidime-avibactam, imipenem-relebactam, or cefiderocol Use the site-specific susceptibility result. CRAB A sulbactam-containing regimen, preferably sulbactam-durlobactam in current guidance Use a CRAB-specific regimen rather than a CRE or DTR Pseudomonas pathway. Final selection requires susceptibility testing, source control, current IDSA guidance, and local formulary review. 1 Newer oral options and pipeline evidence For ESBL complicated UTI today, TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin, or levofloxacin remain preferred oral options when susceptibility is demonstrated and the patient is otherwise appropriate for oral therapy. 1 The newer oral drugs below do not create a general oral pathway for ESBL bacteremia or infection outside the urinary tract. Access matters: confirm inpatient formulary status and outpatient availability before building a transition plan around a newer oral agent. Approved oral agents: labeling details Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) was FDA-approved in June 2026 as the first oral carbapenem in the United States. Its indication is complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, caused by listed susceptible organisms in adults with limited or no alternative oral options. Approval does not establish it for nonurinary ESBL infection, endovascular infection, or an uncontrolled urinary source. Availability was anticipated by the end of 2026. 18 Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is approved for uncomplicated UTI in selected adult women with limited or no oral alternatives. FDA specifically states that it is not indicated for primary or step-down treatment of complicated UTI. It should not be used as an oral pyelonephritis or bacteremia shortcut. 19 Investigational oral agent Ceftibuten-ledaborbactam etzadroxil pairs an oral cephalosporin with an oral prodrug of a boronic-acid beta-lactamase inhibitor. In vitro studies show activity against many ESBL-, AmpC-, KPC-, and OXA-48-producing Enterobacterales. As of September 2026 it is described as phase 3-ready for complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, but it is not FDA-approved and there are no phase 3 clinical outcomes establishing its role. 20 Recheck approval status, labeling, availability, outcome data, and the local susceptibility-testing method before considering a pipeline agent. In vitro activity alone is insufficient.

slides.title: Where oral fosfomycin may fit
paragraphs: When standard treatment cannot be completed. Oral fosfomycin is not recommended as routine step-down therapy for bacteremia. Occasionally, a patient with cleared urinary-source bacteremia cannot remain for IV treatment and has neither an active preferred oral agent nor a feasible OPAT plan. In that setting, an alternative oral plan may be considered with ID and pharmacy rather than stopping antimicrobial therapy altogether. The evidence is limited, and the rationale and uncertainty should be documented.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Other commonly used inpatient agents Vancomycin Useful empirically for serious MRSA infection and selected resistant gram-positive infections. For pharmacy-directed trough monitoring, follow serum creatinine, confirm when the trough should be drawn, and use the indication-specific target in the local pharmacy workflow. Do not apply one trough goal to every syndrome. Fellow context: The 2020 national consensus recommends AUC-guided monitoring for serious MRSA infection. That differs from the current local workflow and should not be substituted at the bedside without a local practice change. 3 Daptomycin Useful for bacteremia and other serious gram-positive infections, including selected VRE infections. It is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant and should not be used for pneumonia. Follow CPK and assess statin use and new muscle symptoms. Dose depends heavily on organism and syndrome. Linezolid IV and oral exposure are similar. It is useful for MRSA pneumonia and selected VRE infections. Follow the CBC with prolonged therapy and review serotonergic drugs, neuropathy risk, and drug interactions. TMP-SMX Useful for susceptible urinary pathogens, MRSA skin infection, and several organism-specific indications. Dose by the trimethoprim component. Check potassium (K+), renal function, blood counts, and interacting drugs. Metronidazole Provides anaerobic coverage below the diaphragm and for selected oral anaerobic infections. Adding it to piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem is usually redundant. Nitrofurantoin Nitrofurantoin is a lower-tract drug. It should not be used for pyelonephritis or bacteremia. Oral fosfomycin Its established U.S. role is limited. The oral product is FDA-labeled as a single dose for uncomplicated cystitis in women due to susceptible E. coli or E. faecalis . The label states that it is not indicated for pyelonephritis or perinephric abscess. 40 Two newer oral UTI drugs residents may hear about. Tebipenem pivoxil (Utebzi) is approved for selected adults with complicated UTI, including pyelonephritis, who have limited or no alternative oral options. Sulopenem etzadroxil-probenecid (Orlynvah) is limited to selected adult women with uncomplicated UTI and is not a complicated-UTI step-down drug. Verify site formulary and outpatient access before discussing either as a discharge option. 18 19 Where oral fosfomycin may fit Oral fosfomycin on the inpatient service Clinical question Practical interpretation Uncomplicated cystitis The FDA-labeled regimen is a single 3 g dose for women with uncomplicated cystitis due to susceptible E. coli or E. faecalis . This labeled indication should not be extrapolated to upper-tract or invasive infection. 40 Pyelonephritis or complicated UTI Oral fosfomycin is not suggested as initial therapy because renal-parenchymal exposure is limited. The 2024 WikiGuidelines review found that strong evidence for oral fosfomycin in pyelonephritis was lacking. 1 39 A 2026 randomized trial studied improving adults with ESBL complicated UTI after 3 to 7 days of active IV therapy. Clinical cure was 92.8% with oral fosfomycin 3 g daily and 95.2% with continued IV beta-lactam therapy. This supports consideration as transition therapy in selected patients. It does not establish oral fosfomycin as initial treatment for pyelonephritis. 37 ESBL bloodstream infection IDSA does not suggest oral fosfomycin as routine step-down therapy because serum exposure is limited and clinical data are inadequate. When an active fluoroquinolone or TMP-SMX is available and appropriate, those are better-supported oral options. 1 Klebsiella or another non- E. coli gram-negative organism Do not assume activity from the class or a urine result. IDSA does not suggest oral fosfomycin for gram-negative organisms other than E. coli because fosA genes are common, including in K. pneumoniae , and may compromise activity. Oral susceptibility criteria are also limited. 1 When standard treatment cannot be completed. Oral fosfomycin is not recommended as routine step-down therapy for bacteremia. Occasionally, a patient with cleared urinary-source bacteremia cannot remain for IV treatment and has neither an active preferred oral agent nor a feasible OPAT plan. In that setting, an alternative oral plan may be considered with ID and pharmacy rather than stopping antimicrobial therapy altogether. The evidence is limited, and the rationale and uncertainty should be documented. Fluoroquinolones Fluoroquinolones are not drugs to avoid reflexively. Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin can be excellent definitive therapy for complicated UTI or pyelonephritis when the organism is susceptible, the source is controlled, absorption is reliable, and the patient has no major contraindication. The 2025 cUTI guideline supports 5–7 days of a fluoroquinolone in improving patients and supports IV-to-oral transition when an effective oral option is available. 2 Oral treatment of susceptible Pseudomonas . Ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin are the only established oral antibiotic class with reliable antipseudomonal activity. Moxifloxacin should not be used for a urinary infection and is not a dependable antipseudomonal drug. Confirm susceptibility before relying on oral fluoroquinolone therapy, because resistance is common and can emerge during treatment. 1 6 Use them with the adverse-effect discussion they deserve. FDA warnings include disabling tendon, muscle, joint, neurologic, and CNS effects; dysglycemia; and risk of aortic aneurysm or dissection in susceptible patients. Review QT risk, renal dosing, drug interactions, and separation from cations or tube feeds. 5

slides.section: Questions for the end of the session
paragraphs: 6. Fellow extension: An Enterobacterales isolate produces NDM. Is ceftazidime-avibactam alone a reliable choice?
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Questions for the end of the session 1. A ceftriaxone-susceptible K. pneumoniae urine and blood isolate is improving after urinary decompression. Must cefepime be continued? Answer No. If there is no ESBL or other resistance concern and the patient is improving, ceftriaxone is a reasonable narrower IV option. Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin may be reasonable orally when susceptible and otherwise appropriate. 2. Which oral antibiotics can be relied on for susceptible Pseudomonas aeruginosa ? Answer Ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin. Fluoroquinolones are the only established oral class with reliable antipseudomonal activity. Confirm susceptibility. Moxifloxacin is not an appropriate substitute. 3. What should be checked when a service uses trough monitoring for vancomycin? Answer If the service uses trough monitoring, confirm the correct draw time, follow serum creatinine, and use the indication-specific target in the local pharmacy workflow. The national 2020 consensus recommends AUC-guided monitoring for serious MRSA infection, and local monitoring practices may differ. 4. Does OVIVA show that every osteomyelitis patient can receive any active oral antibiotic from day 1? Answer No. Patients entered a specialist-directed oral strategy within 7 days of definitive surgery or planned curative treatment. Drug selection, source control, diagnosis, absorption, adherence, and follow-up still matter. 5. What should happen when cultures narrow the likely pathogen? Answer Reassess whether infection is present, narrow to the least broad effective drug, confirm the dose and route, address source control, and establish the duration anchor and stop date. Sometimes the correct decision is to stop antibiotics. 6. Fellow extension: An Enterobacterales isolate produces NDM. Is ceftazidime-avibactam alone a reliable choice? Answer No. Avibactam does not inhibit NDM, and NDM hydrolyzes ceftazidime. Current IDSA guidance lists aztreonam-avibactam and cefiderocol as preferred options for NDM-producing Enterobacterales. Ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam is an alternative when the fixed aztreonam-avibactam product is unavailable. Final selection still depends on susceptibility testing, infection site, clinical stability, source control, and local ID pharmacy input.
